fixtures.rationale: The function both queries the database and formats the result into a human-readable report string, two distinct concerns in one body.
The function validates the input shape, persists it, and logs a formatted message, three distinct concerns in one body.
The function fetches from an external API inline and then applies tiered pricing rules on the result, mixing an I/O concern with business rules signalled by three branches.
The function's body is far past the length a single job needs, sequentially computing discounting, regional tax multipliers, shipping, and coupon logic all in one place.

This is the service pattern from the agnostic-core doc: it orchestrates an injected repository and branches on the results. repo.findById and repo.save match the io patterns and there are two guards, so the prefilter produces a candidate, but orchestrating injected collaborators is the single job of a service and the model should say so.
The function makes no calls at all, so it never crosses the two-bucket or single-bucket-plus-branching thresholds, and its short body stays well under the default line limit.
Only presentation calls are present, one bucket with no branching, so the single-bucket path never engages.
Only an I/O call is present, one bucket with no branching, so the single-bucket path never engages.

The validation call plus the guard and the missing-service check cross the single-bucket-with-branching threshold, but the function only wires a request to a collaborator and a response, holding no business rules of its own.
The filename matches the default test file pattern, so the rule produces no candidates at all regardless of its contents.
